items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: There was one time I sat in with him when I was like you know, twelve or thirteen years old.

ctx.x: Were your tastes then a little bit out of the ordinary with people your own age?

Oh, yeah, I had a few friends that were into jazz you know, but only on certain occasions would I run into a younger musician that could actually play a little bit. There was a gentleman by the name of Bob Mover, an alto saxophone player, we were in seventh and eighth grades together. And we shared a lot of great jazz experience around that time, hanging out with Ira Sullivan down in Florida, and some great players that Ira played with. Ira is one of our great educators. He goes to all the schools and plays, but…
